intent.task: Prove preservation of coprimality and distinguish equality after cancellation from an actual nontrivial reduction.
intent.source_solution: Writing an integer fraction in lowest terms gives n!=0 and gcd(|m|,|n|)=1. Where n+m!=0, gcd(m,n+m)=gcd(m,n)=1, so the first fraction is irreducible. Its denominator can vanish if m=-n; coprimality allows examples m=-1,n=1 or m=1,n=-1. The second denominator is n(1+m), which vanishes for m=-1. Where it is nonzero, gcd(m,n)=1 and gcd(m,m+1)=1 imply gcd(m,n(m+1))=1, so that fraction is also irreducible. The third fraction is n/(5n)=1/5 because n!=0, and gcd(|n|,|5n|)=|n|. It admits a nontrivial reduction exactly when |n|>1; for n=1 or n=-1 it is already in lowest terms. Even under a positive-integer reading, n=1 is not excluded.
